Daily Trading Retrospective — NSE/NIFTY F&O

Date: 2026-09-29

Analyst: Expert Quantitative Trader & Risk Manager

1. Was the selection good for the day?

  • Directional Alignment with Market Breadth:

The broader market exhibited a remarkably flat profile (0.0% of stocks closing in the red, with mean and median returns at 0.0%), and the Nifty index remained tightly range-bound throughout the session. Despite a completely flat macro environment, the high-conviction selection model generated strictly SHORT signals. In a directionless market, forcing short entries without macro/index confirmation exposed the strategy to unnecessary beta friction.

  • Combined Score ≥ 85 Filter Performance:

The filter successfully isolated 8 high-conviction candidates out of a 210-stock F&O universe. Interestingly, despite early stop-loss breaches, 5 out of 8 stocks (62.5%) closed in profit for the short direction at EOD. This indicates that the underlying alpha model possesses sound directional forecasting power over a multi-session or EOD horizon, even if intraday path dependency causes premature stop-outs.

  • Why the Majority Closed Profitable at EOD:

The divergence between intraday failures and EOD success highlights a classic timing and volatility issue. While the model correctly identified assets facing downward pressure, the chosen entry timings and rigid stop-loss thresholds caused positions to be shaken out before the terminal drift manifested in favor of the short thesis.

2. What went well?

  • Standout Alpha Generation (AMBER):

AMBER was the crown jewel of the session, delivering a SUCCESS outcome by plummeting -4.90% from its entry price with a max adverse excursion of 0.0%. This represents an ideal execution where the price moved straight to the -2.0% target without triggering any overhead noise.

  • Positive EOD Drift in Active Trades:

Out of the 4 trades held actively through EOD (BIOCON, GRASIM, MOTILALOFS, INDUSINDBK), 100% were floating in positive territory at market close, led by MOTILALOFS (-0.73%) and GRASIM (-0.54%).

  • Noise Reduction:

Filtering 210 volatile F&O instruments down to just 8 high-conviction names (less than 4% of the universe) demonstrates that the quantitative scoring mechanism effectively zeroes in on relative weakness candidates, preventing capital dispersion across low-alpha noise.

3. What didn't go well?

  • Intraday Failures (ADANIENT, TMPV, JIOFIN):

Three stocks hit the static +1.0% stop loss early in the session. ADANIENT (+2.23% EOD), TMPV (+1.86% EOD), and JIOFIN (+0.94% EOD) demonstrated strong upside momentum right after entry, completely overriding the short thesis.

  • The Asymmetric Risk-Reward Trap (1.0% SL vs. 2.0% Target):

A strict 1.0% Stop Loss combined with a 2.0% Target requires a win rate significantly higher than 67% just to break even on an expected value basis. In an intraday environment characterized by normal market noise and opening volatility, a tight 1.0% stop on high-beta F&O stocks acts as a magnet for whipsaws, cutting winning ideas before they mature.

  • Entry Timing Vulnerability:

Several positions (e.g., TMPV and JIOFIN) were entered right at the market open (10:00:13 AM). Opening ranges are notoriously noisy, frequently trapping momentum traders in fakeouts before the true institutional trend establishes itself post-10:30 AM.

4. What can be done to improve the selection?

  • Volatility-Adjusted / ATR-Based Stop Losses:

Abandon static percentage stops (1%). Instead, scale stop-losses dynamically using the Average True Range (ATR) or intraday volatility bands (e.g., 1.5 × 15-min ATR), allowing high-beta names like ADANIENT room to breathe without violating structural invalidation levels.

  • Liquidity and Intraday VWAP Filters:

Integrate a VWAP confirmation filter for short entries—only permit execution if the price is trading strictly below the volume-weighted average price and below the opening range low.

  • Time-Based Entry Filtering:

Prohibit entries during the chaotic opening 30 minutes (09:15 – 09:45 AM). Delaying execution windows ensures that initial liquidity imbalances clear out, leading to cleaner directional persistence.

5. Recommendations to improve

1. Implement Adaptive Stop Losses: Replace the fixed 1.0% stop-loss rule with a volatility-adjusted dynamic stop (e.g., 1.25 × ATR_{14} on a 15-minute timeframe) to curtail premature stop-outs.
2. Incorporate Macro/Index Filter Gates: Restrict short execution if Nifty breadth or index snapshots are flat-to-bullish, ensuring portfolio alignment with broader market momentum.
3. Staggered Execution Windows: Enforce a blackout period between 09:15 and 09:45 AM. Move entry execution slots to post-opening range formation to filter out early-session price discovery noise.
4. Time-Based Exit / Partial Profit Mechanics: Introduce trailing stops or scale-out targets (e.g., take 50% profit at -1.5%, trail the rest) to lock in gains when stocks experience favorable drift but fail to reach the full -2.0% target.
